29 An electromagnetic wave is diffracted as it passes through a single slit. The width of the slit is
larger than the wavelength of the wave.
Which change will decrease the amount of diffraction of the wave?
A
Decrease the frequency of the wave.
B
Decrease the time period of the wave.
C
Decrease the width of the slit.
D
Increase the wavelength of the wave.

hints: Notice the question asks for less spreading, and significant diffraction needs wavelength $\lambda$ comparable to slit width $w$.
Recall for an electromagnetic wave $c = f\lambda$ and $f = 1/T$, so changing frequency or time period changes $\lambda$.
Compare each change by asking whether $\lambda / w$ gets smaller: smaller $\lambda$ or larger $w$ means less diffraction.
walkthrough: Identify the governing idea: the amount of single-slit diffraction is controlled by the ratio of wavelength to slit width, $\lambda / w$.
Larger $\lambda / w$ means more spreading; smaller $\lambda / w$ means less spreading and a narrower central maximum.
For an electromagnetic wave in air, speed $c$ is fixed, with $c = f\lambda$ and $f = 1/T$, so $\lambda = cT = c/f$.
Decreasing the time period $T$ increases frequency $f$ and therefore decreases wavelength $\lambda$.
With $\lambda$ smaller and slit width $w$ unchanged, $\lambda / w$ is smaller, so the wave spreads less.

A.explanation: Decreasing frequency increases wavelength because $c = f\lambda$, so the ratio $\lambda / w$ increases and diffraction increases.

B.explanation: Decreasing time period increases frequency since $f = 1/T$, so wavelength decreases and the ratio $\lambda / w$ decreases, giving less diffraction.

C.explanation: A narrower slit makes slit width $w$ closer to wavelength $\lambda$, so $\lambda / w$ increases and diffraction increases.

D.explanation: A larger wavelength directly increases $\lambda / w$ for the same slit, so spreading by diffraction increases.
